thread:
lina: Heads-up — Highcrest is pushing back on our Dedicated commitment proposal. They signed for a committed baseline but want a smaller guaranteed GPU-hours number. They say Q3 marketing + seasonal holiday burst is uncertain. Can infra advise on headroom vs fixed buffer policy?

jasper: Short answer: we need a headroom approach, not a flat buffer. Their workload is spiky (short high-throughput windows) so a flat % can either under-provision during spikes or waste capacity most of the time.

alex: Agree with jasper. Also region matters — Highcrest wants EU-only for data residency. EU pool capacity is tighter this quarter because of other Dedicated commitments.

maria: From product/ops perspective, customers prefer predictable price/commit but also an option for controlled burst. We should draft a clear burst pricing addendum.

conor: Financial constraints: their CFO will accept committed pricing if effective utilization >= 75%. If our headroom bumps cost per reserved GPU by >12% they will balk.

lina: Concrete numbers they're discussing: they asked for billing on 150k GPU-hours/mo but want the SLA to cover up to 200k GPU-hours/mo for bursts.

jasper: Quick calc I ran locally:
```
Committed baseline = 150,000 GPU-hours/mo
Requested burst cap = 200,000 GPU-hours/mo
Headroom needed = (200k - 150k) / 150k = 33% extra peak capacity
```
33% headroom is material and not great for EU pool. If we force 33% reserved for them it's going to raise unit costs.

alex: Alternative: keep committed baseline at 150k, allow burst up to 200k but meter bursts at a premium and enforce throttles when cluster-wide contention rises. Also add a "grace reserve" of 10% we can borrow across regions during short spikes.

capacity-bot: Reservation preview for Highcrest: baseline=150000h, soft-burst=200000h, premium-burst-rate=2.3x, grace-reserve=10% (cross-region borrow subject to compliance check).

maria: Compliance flag — cross-region borrow needs legal sign-off for EU data residency. That likely kills cross-region borrow unless Highcrest signs a waiver.

jasper: So realistic options: 1) Baseline 150k + priced burst to 200k at 2.3x (no extra reserved headroom) — minimal infra impact, predictable $$; 2) Reserve 180k (20% headroom) at committed rate with a smaller billed burst above that — higher infra cost but simpler SLA; 3) Hybrid: 150k committed, 10% soft reserve in EU (for short windows) + priced burst and strict throttles.

conor: From finance POV option 1 is cleanest. Pricing math says highcrest effective utilization likely >75% if we keep paid-burst premium ~2x. Option 2 will increase their sticker price ~13-16% which C-suite may reject.

lina: Customer asked about our "buffer" policy earlier docs. We don't have a single canonical number in the EU. What do we operate now?

jasper: Historically infra reserves 15% headroom for small dev pools and 20% for Dedicated in peak regions. But that's been flexible; last quarter we bumped APAC to 30% because of onboarding spikes.

alex: Operational constraints: if we allow 33% effective peak for one tenant in EU it reduces elasticity for other Dedicated customers and increases pre-provisioning lead time for on-demand spikes.

maria: Proposed negotiation language for Lina to offer Highcrest: "We can commit to 150k GPU-hours/month at the standard committed rate, plus a soft-burst allowance to 200k billed at a premium (2.0-2.5x). For regulated EU-only customers, cross-region grace reserves are available only with explicit data transfer agreements."

lina: I'll propose option 1 + a 90-day pilot where we measure actual burst behavior. If they show >85% sustained utilization during pilot we can revisit committed baseline.

conor: Addendum: include a clause for "early adjustment" — if observed utilization >85% for two consecutive months, automatic re-rate / rollback to new committed baseline with 30-day notice.

jasper: Action items: (1) infra to run an EU pool capacity impact sim for a 150->200k burst window lasting up to 72 hours (jasper + alex) — due EOD tomorrow; (2) legal to confirm cross-region waiver language (maria); (3) pricing draft with premium band (conor + maria); (4) lina to propose 90-day pilot to customer.

alex: For the sim I'll need historical spike distributions from Highcrest test runs and current EU Reserved capacity headroom. Lina can you paste their last 3 months' peak windows?

lina: Pasting snippets from their runbook: ``peak windows: 2025-11-20 12:00-16:00 (3.5x baseline qps), 2025-12-05 10:00-18:00 (holiday promo, 5x baseline for 8h)`` — I'll upload logs to the shared drive. :thumbsup:

capacity-bot: New thread task created: "Highcrest EU burst sim" assigned to jasper, alex — due 2025-03-12 17:00 UTC.

maria: thanks everyone. If infra sim shows <10% impact on other Dedicated tenants with the premium-burst route, product is happy to sign off.

lina: Ok I'll present option 1 + pilot tomorrow morning with the customer. Will loop back here after call.

jasper: Good plan. I'll start the sim now and ping once I have baseline numbers.

alex: I'll double-check capacity reservations and make a short note about throttling behavior to include in the SLA (what happens when cluster contention > 90%).

lina: Thanks all — will update after call. :raised_hands:
